summary: The gateway disabled TLS certificate verification AND hostname verification globally for the entire JVM, unconditionally, in every environment - not scoped to Angel One at all. SslConfig.applyGlobalSslBypass() was called from PietraderGatewayApplication.main() before Spring even started, plus a second time from AngelTokenService.loadFromUrl(); AngelWebSocketClient installed an identical trust-all TrustManager directly on the WebSocket client; two further dead duplicate copies of the same pattern (SslBypass.java, SslUtil.java) existed unused. The existing SslConfigTest actively asserted this dangerous behaviour as correct (e.g. asserting the hostname verifier accepted any host).

fix: Removed the applyGlobalSslBypass() call and the method itself; removed the inline WebSocket trust-all block; removed the AngelTokenService call site; deleted the two dead duplicate classes. SslConfig now only provides a plain RestTemplate bean. Documented in SslConfig's class javadoc what to do if a real PKIX error recurs against a live Angel One connection (not verified in this sandbox - no network path to Angel One here): add the specific CA to a dedicated truststore, never reintroduce a bypass.
